threads.body: The Java example mixes a separate `String name` parameter with a `TestCase` that also contains `name`, and the `name` method parameter is otherwise unused. This is easy for readers to copy/paste into real tests where Error Prone can flag unused parameters, and it also creates a risk of the display name diverging from `TestCase.name`. Consider restructuring the example to pass a single `TestCase` argument (and rely on `TestCase.toString()` / an overridden record `toString()` for the display name), or remove the `name` component from `TestCase` if the standalone `String name` is the recommended pattern.

Align the narrative + example so the `{0}` placeholder consistently refers to the same kind of argument (either the name string or the test-case object).
